clauses.text: The school day runs outdoors as normal unless a clause below applies.
No vigorous outdoor activity once forecast PM2.5 passes 90 (CPCB Moderate ceiling), because exertion roughly triples the inhaled dose.
No outdoor activity at all once forecast PM2.5 passes 120 (CPCB Very Poor).
A class carrying children on the respiratory register stays indoors once forecast PM2.5 passes 60, India's NAAQS 24-hour standard.
No outdoor activity when the mixing layer is below 500 m and PM2.5 is already above 60: trapped air gets worse through the session.
An activity does not stay outdoors when moving it would avoid more than 50 ug.h of inhaled dose - a third of a child's WHO weekly budget, recoverable today.
Once a class has taken 100 ug.h today - two thirds of a WHO week in one day - the rest of its outdoor periods come inside.

Classroom windows shut once forecast PM2.5 passes 60 (NAAQS). The indoor fallback only reduces dose if the windows are actually shut, so this clause is what makes moving a class indoors mean anything.
Masks are issued to the respiratory register once PM2.5 passes 90, and to every child once it passes 120.
